response.text:
### Given data

\[
(x_i,y_i)=(-5,-2),(-3,1),(0,4),(2,6),(1,3), \qquad n=5.
\]

The least-squares estimates in the simple linear regression model are

\[
\hat\beta_1=\frac{S_{xy}}{S_{xx}}, \qquad 
\hat\beta_0=\bar y-\hat\beta_1\bar x.
\]

Compute

\[
\bar x=\frac{-5-3+0+2+1}{5}=-1,
\qquad
\bar y=\frac{-2+1+4+6+3}{5}=\frac{12}{5}=2.4.
\]

Also,

\[
S_{xx}=\sum (x_i-\bar x)^2=34,
\]

and

\[
S_{xy}=\sum (x_i-\bar x)(y_i-\bar y)=34.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\hat\beta_1=\frac{34}{34}=1,
\]

and

\[
\hat\beta_0=\bar y-\hat\beta_1\bar x=2.4-1(-1)=3.4=\frac{17}{5}.
\]

So the fitted regression line is

\[
\boxed{\hat y=3.4+x}
\]

or equivalently

\[
\boxed{\hat y=\frac{17}{5}+x.}
\]

---

## (1) Estimates and scatterplot with fitted line

\[
\boxed{\hat\beta_0=3.4,\qquad \hat\beta_1=1.}
\]

The fitted line is

\[
\hat y=x+3.4.
\]

A schematic scatterplot with the fitted line is:

```
y
6 |                         ●
5 |                      /
4 |                 ●   /
3 |                    ●
2 |              /
1 |      ●     /
0 |          /
-1|       /
-2|●    /
   +--------------------------
    -5  -4  -3  -2  -1   0   1   2    x
```

The dots are the observed data points, and the line represents \(\hat y=x+3.4\).

---

## (2) Fitted values \(\hat y_i\)

Using

\[
\hat y_i=3.4+x_i,
\]

we get:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
i & x_i & y_i & \hat y_i \\ \hline
1 & -5 & -2 & -1.6 \\
2 & -3 & 1 & 0.4 \\
3 & 0 & 4 & 3.4 \\
4 & 2 & 6 & 5.4 \\
5 & 1 & 3 & 4.4
\end{array}
\]

Thus,

\[
\boxed{\hat y=(-1.6,\;0.4,\;3.4,\;5.4,\;4.4).}
\]

---

## (3) Residuals and residual plot

The residuals are

\[
e_i=y_i-\hat y_i.
\]

Thus,

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
i & x_i & y_i & \hat y_i & e_i=y_i-\hat y_i \\ \hline
1 & -5 & -2 & -1.6 & -0.4 \\
2 & -3 & 1 & 0.4 & 0.6 \\
3 & 0 & 4 & 3.4 & 0.6 \\
4 & 2 & 6 & 5.4 & 0.6 \\
5 & 1 & 3 & 4.4 & -1.4
\end{array}
\]

So

\[
\boxed{e=(-0.4,\;0.6,\;0.6,\;0.6,\;-1.4).}
\]

A residual plot versus \(x\) is:

```
residual
 0.6 |        ●          ●      ●
 0.0 |--------------------------------
-0.4 |  ●
-1.4 |                      ●
      +--------------------------------
        -5       -3      0      1   2     x
```

---

## (4) Compute \(R^2\)

We use

\[
R^2=1-\frac{\text{SSE}}{\text{SST}},
\]

where

\[
\text{SSE}=\sum e_i^2.
\]

From the residuals,

\[
\text{SSE}=(-0.4)^2+(0.6)^2+(0.6)^2+(0.6)^2+(-1.4)^2.
\]

Thus,

\[
\text{SSE}=0.16+0.36+0.36+0.36+1.96=3.2.
\]

Also,

\[
\text{SST}=\sum (y_i-\bar y)^2.
\]

Since \(\bar y=2.4\),

\[
\text{SST}=(-2-2.4)^2+(1-2.4)^2+(4-2.4)^2+(6-2.4)^2+(3-2.4)^2.
\]

So

\[
\text{SST}=19.36+1.96+2.56+12.96+0.36=37.2.
\]

Therefore,

\[
R^2=1-\frac{3.2}{37.2}
=1-\frac{16/5}{186/5}
=1-\frac{16}{186}
=1-\frac{8}{93}
=\frac{85}{93}.
\]

Hence,

\[
\boxed{R^2=\frac{85}{93}\approx 0.914.}
\]

\[

\[
